outlook.statement: India's domestic economic activity remains strong and is expected to continue on a robust trajectory. RBI has projected real GDP growth for FY 2026-27 at 6.9%. IMF projects India's calendar year 2026 GDP growth at 6.5%. NBFC sector credit growth projected to sustain 15-17% annual pace through FY28. Industry observers expect NBFC sector profits to nearly double by FY30.

risks: Slowdown in global and Indian economy triggered by Middle East conflict, elevated energy prices, and geopolitical tensions
Renewed inflationary pressures due to higher global commodity and energy prices constraining monetary policy easing
Potential slowdown in real estate sector impacting collections and loan book growth
Challenges in raising funds at competitive borrowing costs for smaller and mid-sized NBFCs
Execution risks associated with business verticals and newly launched unsecured loan products
Regulatory compliance requirements under RBI's evolving Scale-Based Regulation framework
High cost of funds for smaller NBFCs amid tight liquidity conditions
Rising Non-Performing Assets (NPAs) particularly in unsecured retail lending segments
Competition from other NBFCs, banks, and new-age fintech lenders
Global geopolitical risks particularly rising energy prices due to Middle East conflict
The Company is exposed to the risk of price fluctuation of raw materials as well as finished goods.
Market risk comprising interest rate risk, currency risk and other price risk
Credit risk from financing activities, including deposits with banks and financial institutions and other financial instruments
Liquidity risk managed through long term bank loans, short term borrowings and finance leases
